purpose: This medicine is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines two different medicines into one pill to make it easier to manage your diabetes. It is usually used along with a healthy diet and regular exercise.
how_it_works: Metformin works by reducing the amount of sugar your liver releases into your blood and helping your body use insulin more effectively. Saxagliptin works by boosting natural hormones in your body that tell your pancreas to release more insulin after you eat and reduce the amount of sugar your liver makes. Together, these two medicines team up to keep your blood sugar levels in a healthier range throughout the day.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and stomach pain, especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice a runny nose, headache, or upper respiratory infections. Taking the medicine with food can help reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: A rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis can occur with metformin — signs include muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, or feeling very weak, so contact your doctor right away if you notice these. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as this medicine may not be right for you. It may also rarely cause serious allergic reactions or joint pain. Do not drink excessive alcohol while taking this medicine. Your doctor will need to temporarily stop this medicine if you are having surgery or certain medical imaging tests with contrast dye.
typical_dosing: The typical dose is one tablet taken twice daily with meals to help reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will determine the right strength based on your current blood sugar control and kidney function. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never adjust your dose on your own.
